prompt_text: Write a Python solution for the GeeksforGeeks problem 'Card Flip'. Determine the minimum number of operations required to arrange cards so that the numbers on the visible sides are in non-decreasing order after swap and flip operations.
actual_output: Time Limit Exceeded (10 / 1114 test cases passed)

bug_analysis.bug_description: The solution uses BFS over all permutations and flip states of cards. For n up to 16, the state space grows to O(n! * 2^n), which is too large and causes the algorithm to exceed the time limit.
bug_analysis.root_cause: Brute-force exploration of permutation and flip parity states instead of using the expected O(2^n) bitmask dynamic programming approach.
bug_analysis.bug_location: Breadth-first search loop exploring all permutations of cards.

test_failures.details: Only 10 out of 1114 test cases passed before timeout.

improvement_strategy.improvements_made: Replace BFS state exploration with bitmask DP tracking used cards and visible values.
